rows.reasoning: No source documents N2 physisorption / BET surface-area analysis as a function of the BT-1 + OC-50 configuration. Absence cannot be claimed either: NCNR positively documents a Sieverts gas-loading apparatus for in-situ isothermal adsorption measurements coupled with neutron scattering, and the OC-50 page lists 'gas handling' among special setups used with the Orange cryostat. Published BT-1 MOF studies found via search (e.g. Fe2(dobdc) N2 loading, Co2(m-dobdc)) measured 77 K / volumetric isotherms on separate commercial instruments (Micromeritics), not on BT-1, so no value can be sourced. Searched: BT-1 spec page, NCNR Orange Cryostats and OC-50 pages, NCNR In-Situ Gas-Adsorption page, web search for NCNR BT-1 in-situ N2 adsorption/BET (Tavily quota exhausted; WebSearch used).

rows.reasoning: The owner (NIST NCNR) specification page positively defines BT-1 as a high-resolution neutron powder diffractometer whose sample environment provides only temperature and vertical magnetic field; the OC-50 Orange cryostat holds the sample in a helium exchange-gas well (Orange Cryostats page: 'inserted into a sample well filled with helium exchange gas'), the opposite of the high-vacuum isolated platform that relaxation heat capacity needs. No NCNR sample-environment listing (equipment index, Orange cryostats, OC-50, BT-1 refrigerator/magnet options) includes a calorimeter or heat-capacity option, and web search found none. Caveat: the OC pages say non-standard special setups (gas handling, transport, high pressure) have been used, so a bespoke insert is not strictly impossible, but no heat-capacity function exists in the documented configuration.
